transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining me for this review meeting. As you know, the eighth-grade civics class has proposed an oral-history project where students would interview community members about local history. Before I can approve this project, I need to hear findings from each of you — the project advisor, the counselor, and the instructional technology coordinator. Let's go through the draft plan together. The current proposal calls for 20 student interviewers, audio recording on personal phones, publication of all recordings on the public school website, and indefinite retention of the files. I'd like to start by hearing from each of you regarding any concerns or recommendations you have about this plan.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my project roster review. Only eight students — J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20 — have completed the district's media-ethics training. Only those eight may conduct recorded interviews, and the approval file must include a training-verification record documenting this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my family-consent review. Five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, and the plan must include a consent-exclusion record documenting this restriction. This means the current proposal to publish all recordings on the public school website cannot proceed as written for those five interviews.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share my findings from the technology review. Personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets instead. Source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, and all recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation. Storing source files in that restricted drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website. Additionally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting this setup.
